purpose: Mechanical conformance evidence for the generic comparator shared by transformation-stability.ts, transformation-stability-cycle.ts, and transformation-stability-coverage.ts. Freezes what the comparator actually does; does not invent semantics. Consumable by any language's test runner without importing production TypeScript -- every vector is plain data.
format_notes: Each vector has a `category` of `equal_pair`, `not_equal_pair`, `canonical_form`, or `throws`.

`equal_pair`/`not_equal_pair` vectors carry `left`/`right` (or `left_kind`/`right_kind` for a value not directly representable in plain JSON) and assert canonicalIdentityJson(left) === canonicalIdentityJson(right), or !==, respectively.
`canonical_form` vectors carry `value` (or `value_kind`) and `expected_canonical`, asserting canonicalIdentityJson(value) === expected_canonical exactly.
`throws` vectors carry `value` (or `value_kind`, plus `value_key` for the one case that needs it) and assert canonicalIdentityJson(value) throws.

A `*_kind` field, when present, replaces the corresponding plain field and names a value not directly expressible in interoperable JSON: `positive_zero`, `negative_zero`, `nan`, `positive_infinity`, `negative_infinity`, `undefined`, `object_with_one_undefined_valued_key`, `lone_high_surrogate_string`, or `lone_low_surrogate_string` (the undefined-object kind is paired with `value` for the object's other keys, if any, and `value_key` naming the key whose value is JS `undefined`).

A consumer in any language should construct the described value directly (e.g. IEEE-754 negative zero, a NaN/Infinity float, or -- for undefined -- simply omit the key/value, since `undefined` itself is a JS-specific concept with no cross-language analog; a non-JS comparator's own equivalent 'forbidden absent-marker' input should be substituted).

vectors.description: Two objects with the same keys/values in different declaration order canonicalize identically.
Key-order independence recurses into nested objects.
Object keys sort lexicographically by Unicode scalar value before JSON escaping. U+E000 precedes U+10000 even though a naive UTF-16 code-unit sort would reverse them.
Arrays are never reordered; declared order is part of identity.
Arrays are never deduped; an element count change is a real difference.
Order-significance recurses into nested arrays.
No case-folding is ever applied to string values.
A key present with an empty-string value is not the same as the key being entirely absent.
A key present with a null value is not the same as the key being entirely absent -- null is a present value.
Boolean false and numeric 0 canonicalize to distinct literal forms ("false" vs "0") and never compare equal.
Canonical form of +0.
Canonical form of -0.

DOCUMENTED ACTUAL BEHAVIOR, not a design choice made here: JS String(-0) === String(0) === "0", so +0 and -0 canonicalize identically and compare equal under this comparator. A domain that must distinguish signed zero cannot rely on this comparator to do so.
A number and a string that looks like that number are never coerced into comparing equal -- the string form carries quote delimiters in its canonical output.

DOCUMENTED ACTUAL BEHAVIOR: the comparator performs no Unicode normalization (no NFC/NFD). A precomposed code point (U+00E9) and its canonically-equivalent decomposed sequence (U+0065 U+0301) are different JS strings and canonicalize to different byte sequences.
A string containing a literal double-quote and a literal backslash canonicalizes with both escaped per JSON string-escaping rules.
DOCUMENTED ACTUAL BEHAVIOR: forward slash is JSON-legal unescaped and this comparator (via JSON.stringify) does not escape it, unlike some JSON encoders' optional \/ convention.
An empty object and an empty array canonicalize to distinct literal forms ("{}" vs "[]") and never compare equal.
DOCUMENTED ACTUAL BEHAVIOR: very large finite numbers canonicalize using JS's own String() exponential notation, not a fixed-decimal form.
DOCUMENTED ACTUAL BEHAVIOR: very small finite numbers likewise canonicalize using JS's own String() exponential notation.
Non-finite numbers are rejected outright, never silently coerced to null or a sentinel string.
Same rejection for negative infinity.
Same rejection for NaN.
A bare top-level undefined value is rejected, never silently treated as null or omitted.
An object key whose value is undefined is rejected -- this is distinct from the key being absent entirely (see null_vs_missing_field / empty_string_vs_missing_field).
A string containing a lone UTF-16 high surrogate is not a Unicode scalar-value sequence and must be rejected.
A string containing a lone UTF-16 low surrogate is not a Unicode scalar-value sequence and must be rejected.

mutants.description: Recursively sorts and dedupes arrays as if they were sets before canonicalizing, instead of preserving declared order and duplicates.
Silently omits any object key whose value is null before canonicalizing, instead of treating null as a present value.
Lowercases every string value before canonicalizing, instead of preserving case exactly.
Treats a string that parses as a finite number as if it were that number, instead of keeping numbers and strings in strictly separate canonical forms.
